title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid regional thrashing
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production incidents on 2026-02-17/18 showed SLO enforcer thrashing between regions when transient latency spikes coincided with regional load imbalance causing repeated regional failovers. This hotfix tightens CB hysteresis and smoothing windows, adjusts load-shedding thresholds for high-priority routes, adds a short backoff before re-enabling a previously failed region, and includes additional metrics/alerts to detect oscillation. Changes include: 1) increase cb.hysteresis_ms from 5000->15000 for regional enforcer, 2) apply exponential backoff on region re-enable attempts starting at 30s->5min capped at 15min, 3) change load_shed.priority_cutoff from 0.6->0.7 and add per-route override whitelist for latency-critical routes, 4) add metrics cb.region_reenable_attempts, cb.region_state_transitions and a new alert SRE/CB-OSCILLATION for >5 transitions in 10m. Testing: unit tests for hysteresis/backoff logic, integration canary in us-west-2 for 2h, manual failover sim using perf-canary harness. Rollout: staged canary (10% traffic us-west-2) -> 50% -> global, with automatic rollback if SLO delta >1.5% after 10m. Related: Linear ENG-1345, incident SUP-8122. This PR is a hotfix and should be merged via squash to main and cherry-picked to release/2026-02.
commits: fix(cb): bump hysteresis and smoothing window for regional enforcer
feat(cb): exponential backoff on region re-enable attempts
fix(load-shed): raise priority cutoff and add per-route whitelist
test(cb): unit tests for hysteresis/backoff behavior
docs: add runbook notes for CB oscillation alert
